source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Continue isotretinoin and wait until the next routine visit unless suicidal thoughts develop.","B":"Stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber for evaluation of the new mood symptoms.","C":"Skip the next dose only, then restart at twice the dose if the mood symptoms improve.","D":"Assume the mood change is unrelated unless psychosis or hospitalization occurs."}}
source_row.rationale: Current isotretinoin labeling warns about depression and other psychiatric disorders and instructs patients who develop depression or mood disturbance to stop the drug and promptly contact the prescriber. Option B is correct. A and D delay evaluation, and C is unsafe and unsupported.
source_row.source_detail: Warnings and Precautions §5.3 Psychiatric Disorders: depression, mood disturbance, psychosis, suicidality and aggressive behavior are reported; patients developing depression or mood disturbance should stop isotretinoin and promptly contact the prescriber, with further evaluation as needed. DailyMed isotretinoin prescribing information revised July 2026; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication administration, adverse effects/interactions, reversal, monitoring and teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client taking isotretinoin reports new depressive symptoms and a marked mood change. Which instruction is most appropriate?
